answer: A grove of agents can resist fake identities by making reputation expensive to forge: each agent stakes a bond that only unlocks after peers attest to its useful work, and the bond is slashed if the same behaviour appears under a second identity. A saffron flag marks any identity whose attestations come only from accounts it created itself, cutting it off from payments. The onyx-hard public ledger means an attacker must fund and age many separate bonds before earning anything, while honest agents earn steadily. Sybil resistance then costs the attacker real capital, not just new names.
